symptoms: Bleeding above the ligament of Treitz.
Clinical features: Haematemesis, Melena stools, Haematochezia, Syncope, Epigastric/abdo pain, Heartburn/dyspepsia.
Glasgow Blatchford Score (GBS): 0 = early D/C, <2 = low risk, >6 = high risk.

management_steps.details: ABCs, Large bore IV lines, Warmed IV fluids, Fluid/blood warmer, Bair-hugger. TRANSFUSE Packed cells +/- blood products.

Contact surgeon early. Pantoprazole 80mg IV STAT + Pantoprazole infusion 80mg in 200ml N/S @ 20ml/hr. Immediate endoscopy, ICU/HCA bed request for admission. If Moderate risk: Pantoprazole 40mg IV STAT, Urgent endoscopy within 24 hrs of admission.
Prophylactic Antibiotics: Ceftriaxone 1G IVI STAT. Consider balloon tamponade.
GBS = 0 early D/C. Book outpatient endoscopy & F/U. Script for PPIs, risk modification.

warnings: Danger groups: Elderly, Varices, Shocked, Fresh blood, Comorbidities, Re-bleeds.
